paper.citation: M. D. Mermelstein, K. Brar, C. Headley, "RIN transfer measurement and modeling in dual-order Raman fiber amplifiers," J. Lightwave Technol. 21(6), 1518-1523 (2003).

notes: Table I is an image in the PDF, not extractable text. Every value under `parameters` was read from a 160 dpi rendering of page 4.

The running text of Section III states launched powers of 760 mW and 22 mW; Table I states 780 mW and 20 mW. Table I is used here because it is what produced the published simulation curves. See `discrepancies`.

discrepancies.reason: Table I is the parameter set used for the published simulation curves in Figs. 5 and 6.

eq_2_walkoff.description: d_31 = 1/v3 -/+ 1/v1 and d_32 = 1/v3 -/+ 1/v2, with v_i = c/n_i. Upper sign co-propagating, lower sign counter-propagating.

group_index.dimensional_problem: The printed form is dimensionally inconsistent: (lambda - lambda_0^2/lambda)^2 has units of length squared, so S_0/8 would have to carry inverse length squared, whereas the dispersion slope has units of time per length cubed. An implicit conversion is therefore present in the printed expression.
group_index.resolution: Use the derived relation d(n_g)/d(lambda) = c * D(lambda) with D(lambda) = S_0 * (lambda - lambda_0), which integrates to n_g(lambda) = n_0 + (c * S_0 / 2) * (lambda - lambda_0)^2. With S_0 in ps/(km nm^2) and lambda in nm this is n_0 + 1.5e-7 * S_0 * (lambda - lambda_0)^2.

check_value.source: Derived from the Mermelstein 2003 Table I parameters via the resolved group-index relation; standard single-mode fiber has a group index near 1.468 at 1550 nm
check_value.note: At 1560 nm with n_0 = 1.466, lambda_0 = 1312 nm and S_0 = 0.088 ps/(km nm^2). Using the printed form directly with S_0 = 0.088 gives 2293, which is not a group index.

eq_5_steady_state.description: Three coupled steady-state power equations for the second-order pump P1, the first-order pump P2, and the signal P3.
eq_5_steady_state.eq_5a: dP1/dz = -alpha_1 P1 - gamma_12 P1 P2 - gamma_13 P1 P3
eq_5_steady_state.eq_5b_as_printed: dP2/dz = -alpha_2 P2 + gamma_12 P1 P2 - gamma_23 P1 P3
eq_5_steady_state.eq_5c: dP3/dz = -/+ alpha_3 P3 +/- gamma_13 P1 P3 +/- gamma_23 P2 P3, upper sign co-propagating
eq_5_steady_state.transcription_issue: Eq. 5b as printed depletes P2 by gamma_23 * P1 * P3, while Eq. 5c gains the signal by gamma_23 * P2 * P3. The pair is not consistent: the same Raman interaction should appear with the same channel pair on both sides. Eq. 5a and Eq. 5c are consistent for gamma_12 (P1 P2) and gamma_13 (P1 P3), which makes the gamma_23 P1 in Eq. 5b a probable typographical error for gamma_23 P2.
eq_5_steady_state.resolution: Implement the self-consistent form, dP2/dz = -alpha_2 P2 + gamma_12 P1 P2 - gamma_23 P2 P3, which pairs gamma_23 P2 P3 with Eq. 5c and is the only version that keeps the Raman interactions pairwise symmetric. Verified at 300 dpi against the printed page 2.
eq_5_steady_state.impact: Using the printed Eq. 5b makes the first-order pump over-deplete and breaks the symmetry that makes the photon-flux conservation diagnostic meaningful.

eq_6_modulation.eq_6a: dm1/dz + i Omega d_31 m1 = -gamma_12 P2 m2 - gamma_13 P3 m3
eq_6_modulation.eq_6b: dm2/dz + i Omega d_32 m2 = +gamma_12 P1 m1 - gamma_23 P3 m3
eq_6_modulation.eq_6c: dm3/dz = +/- gamma_13 P1 m1 +/- gamma_23 P2 m2, upper sign co-propagating
eq_6_modulation.note: Eq. 6b carries the same gamma_23 * P3 * m3 term on the right as a corrected Eq. 5b would, but driven by the modulation index m3 rather than by a power. The perturbation structure therefore also pairs m2 with m3 for gamma_23.

eq_7_transfer.description: Complex RIN transfer from pump i to the signal. M3(L, Omega) = H_3i(L, Omega) * Mi(0, Omega) for co-pump, where the signal is injected at z = 0; for counter-pump the signal is injected at z = L and evaluated at z = 0. Pumps are at z = 0 in both cases.

eq_10_double_pole.description: Trial double-pole fit function whose dc level and 6 dB corner frequency are reported for each measured transfer function.

interaction_lengths.note: Read by eye from Fig. 7. Treated as a mechanism check rather than a hard numeric gate; see the change design doc, Open Questions.

acceptance.justification: DC within 0.5 dB and corner within 20 percent are tight enough that a wrong walk-off sign or a missing loss term fails, and loose enough not to be knife-edge.

reproduction_status.recorded: 2026-10-04 implementation session for the add-raman-rin-transfer-analytics change, updated 2026-10-04 after the Eq. 6 no-self-term fix
reproduction_status.convention: Observed values come from examples/44_cw_cascade_rin_transfer.py and tests/test_raman_transfer.py. Targets are never refitted to match.

reproduced.note: Mermelstein's running text says approximately 13 dB.

Reproduced after reading the printed Eqs. 6 literally: the no-self-term modulation equations are the exact linearization for a RELATIVE modulation index, because the steady-state net gain multiplies mean and fluctuation by the same factor and cancels. The earlier (wrong) self-term addition gave 17.8 dB.

Former structural miss. The paper puts the first-order transfer about 15 dB below the second-order; the printed model returns 14.3 dB, where the self-term version returned 0.8 dB with both DC levels 18 dB high.

Corner read as the 6 dB drop below the response's own DC level; the model response is not exactly double-pole, and the published corners are double-pole fits of measured data, so fit-to-fit comparison over-reads both. The previous 1314 Hz match was obtained with the wrong self-term equations and reproduced by coincidence of a different response shape.

not_reproduced.note: Measured as the e-folding decay of the first-order pump's modulation profile, from its peak.
With the printed no-self-term equations the indirect profile no longer crosses the 37 percent threshold anywhere on the span.

reproduction_status.guard_policy: The DC and corner regressions are now real assertions (DC within 2 dB, 6 dB drop point within 35 percent). The interaction lengths remain pytest.mark.xfail(strict=False); no threshold was loosened to make a passing test.
